runs.question: How did engine_getBlobs response time scale with blob count for each execution client on mainnet on 8 June 2026 (UTC)?
runs.answer:
Here are the results from `mainnet.int_engine_get_blobs` on June 8, 2026 (UTC):

**Response time scales roughly linearly with blob count for all 6 execution clients, but with markedly different slopes:**

| EL Client | Avg @ 1 blob | Avg @ 6 blobs | Avg @ 12 blobs | Avg @ 21 blobs | Slope |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Besu** | 3.9 ms | 19.7 ms | 31.3 ms | 32.2 ms | ~2.2 ms/blob |
| **Nethermind** | 1.6 ms | 12.6 ms | 18.3 ms | 24.0 ms | ~1.1 ms/blob |
| **Reth** | 2.3 ms | 6.1 ms | 12.2 ms | 22.8 ms | ~1.1 ms/blob |
| **ethrex** | 2.0 ms | 8.5 ms | 16.0 ms | 30.9 ms | ~1.5 ms/blob |
| **go-ethereum** | 6.2 ms | 62.6 ms | 108.3 ms | 179.0 ms | ~8.7 ms/blob |
| **erigon** | 7.5 ms | 60.9 ms | 104.8 ms | 174.2 ms | ~8.4 ms/blob |

**Key findings:**
- **Besu, Nethermind, Reth, and ethrex** are fast — all under ~40 ms avg even at 21 blobs, with near-linear scaling at 1-2 ms per additional blob
- **go-ethereum (Geth) and erigon** are ~4-8x slower — avg response time reaches ~180 ms at 21 blobs, scaling at ~8-9 ms per blob
- **erigon** had the highest absolute latency (e.g. 174 ms avg at 21 blobs), while **Nethermind** and **Reth** had the lowest overall

runs.question: How much does block payload size affect block propagation time on mainnet?
runs.answer:
Here are the findings from the analysis of **50,267 mainnet blocks over 7 days**:

**The relationship is weak but measurable.** The Pearson correlation between block payload size and first-seen propagation time is **r ≈ 0.17** — block size explains only ~3% of the variance.

**Key numbers:**
- **Sub-100KB blocks**: median propagation ~1,120ms
- **300-400KB blocks**: median propagation ~1,650ms
- **Larger than 500KB (rare)**: median propagation ~1,600-1,700ms
- P95 stays fairly flat at ~3,000-3,200ms across all sizes
- The effect is roughly **+500ms** going from the smallest to the largest blocks

**Other metrics correlate similarly:**
- `execution_payload_gas_used`: r = 0.18
- `execution_payload_transactions_count`: r = 0.12
- `execution_payload_blob_gas_used`: r = 0.11
- The number of observing nodes doesn't confound the result

**Conclusion:** Block payload size has a statistically significant but practically **weak** effect on propagation time. Other factors — geographic distance between peers, client implementation, network topology, I/O wait from blob sidecars — dominate the variance. Even the largest blocks (>500KB) still reach the network median node within ~1.7s, well within the 4s slot deadline.

- Scatter (5000 sampled slots): `uploaded.url` from first call
- Binned trend (20KB buckets, median/mean/P95): `uploaded.url` from second call

runs.subject: opencode:opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash:cli
runs.question: Around the 3rd-4th of December 2025, MEV relay circuit breakers reportedly tripped on mainnet and relay-delivered blocks collapsed for a while. Find the actual window and quantify how bad it got.
runs.answer:
Here's what I found from the `xatu-cbt` dataset (ClickHouse refined, finalized chain):

---

### Incident Window

The MEV relay circuit breaker event unfolded over **~15 hours**, from **2025-12-03 21:00 UTC** to **2025-12-04 12:00 UTC**, with the absolute worst collapse at **03:00–05:00 UTC on Dec 4**.

| Phase | Period (UTC) | Missed Slots/hr | Missed Rate | MEV Relay-Delivered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Normal baseline (prior days) | — | 0–4 | 0–1.3% | ~92–95% of canonical |
| Onset | Dec 3 21:00–23:00 | 11–19 | 3.7–6.3% | 86–92% (already dipping) |
| **Peak collapse** | **Dec 4 03:00–04:00** | **77, 62** | **25.7%, 20.7%** | **35% of canonical** |
| Trough 5-min buckets | Dec 4 03:25–03:55 | — | — | **0–5.9%** (several zero-MEV buckets) |
| Recovery | Dec 4 05:00–11:00 | 7–20 | 2.3–6.7% | 60–90% (gradual) |
| Back to normal | Dec 4 12:00+ | 1–6 | 0.3–2% | ~90%+ |

### How Bad It Got

- **300 missed slots total** during the 15-hour window vs. a baseline of ~41 over the same length of normal time — a **7× increase**.
- At its worst (03:00–04:00 UTC), **1 in 4 slots** was missed entirely.
- MEV relay delivery collapsed from ~92% of canonical blocks to **~35%** (03:00–05:00 UTC). Several 5-minute windows saw **zero relay-delivered blocks**.

| Relay | Hour 02 | Hour 03 (trough) | Drop |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ultra Sound | 128 | 44 | −66% |
| Titan Relay | 94 | 30 | −68% |
| BloXroute Max Profit | 84 | 35 | −58% |
| BloXroute Regulated | 52 | 25 | −52% |
| Agnostic Gnosis | 25 | 7 | −72% |
| Aestus | 11 | 8 | −27% |
| Flashbots | 14 | 14 | (flat) |
| EthGas | 8 | 3 | −63% |

### Root Cause Context

Bid values during the collapse (p50 ~0.013 ETH, p90 ~0.051 ETH) were not unusually low compared to normal hours — the circuit breakers likely tripped on **profitability thresholds rather than absolute value**. Builders stopped submitting to relays when conditions (possibly base fee dynamics or mempool composition) made their MEV bundles unprofitable below configured minimums, causing a cascading effect as more relays' circuit breakers fired, compounding the block production gap.

The real event window is **2025-12-04 ~02:50 to ~04:50 UTC** (not Dec 3), with the most severe collapse at **03:30–04:00 UTC**.

Key measurements:

| Period | MEV blocks/10min | MEV share | vs. baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline (02–03 Dec) | ~44 | ~85% | — |
| Pre-collapse (02:00–03:00 Dec 4) | 39.7 | 84.7% | normal |
| **Collapse (03:00–05:00)** | **12.8** | **35.6%** | **-85% MEV** |
| **Trough (03:50)** | **5 of 37 slots** | **13.5%** | **-87pp MEV share** |
| Recovery (05:00–06:00) | 35.2 | 80.5% | near normal |

**Severity:** MEV-relayed blocks dropped **~85%** from the baseline rate. At the 03:50 trough, only **5 of 37** canonical slots were relay-delivered (13.5% MEV share vs. typical ~85%). The total canonical block rate also fell (433 vs. expected ~600 over the 2-hour window), indicating missed slots as proposers fell back to local building. All major relays (Ultra Sound, Titan, BloXroute, Flashbots) were affected roughly proportionally. Full recovery took about 2 hours.
